race_context: The district: the state list's 'Martin Shoals School Board' is the Shoals Community School Corporation in Shoals, Martin County, which runs an elementary school, a middle school and a high school {sh_home}{in_list}. State enrollment data show 595 students in 2026, down from 689 in 2022 {idoe_enroll}. At the September 10, 2026 board meeting the superintendent reported 554 K-12 students {sh_min_2026_09_10}.

Superintendent: the board approved Regina Sue Lanham as superintendent effective July 1, 2025, succeeding Superintendent Kindra Hovis {sh_min_2025_04_24}{sh_min_2025_05_22}. Minutes now refer to her as Dr. Sue Lanham {sh_min_2025_12_29}.

Board: the Board of School Trustees has five members. As listed by the district they are Drexel Turpin (president), Eva George (vice president), Annette Taylor (secretary), Lorna Troutman and Ethan Jones {sh_board}. State results list the races by district, Districts 1 through 5, each electing one member {enr_2022}{enr_2024}. Jones (District 2) resigned in August 2026, and on August 24, 2026 the board appointed Angela Cook to the open seat {sh_min_2026_08_13}{sh_min_2026_08_24}{enr_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: Districts 1 and 4, one seat each, which matches the state list {in_list}. Both seats were last filled in 2022, when Annette Taylor (District 1) and Eva N. George (District 4) were each elected without opposition {enr_2022}. Taylor is not on the 2026 ballot, so District 1 is an open seat contested by Courtney Cave and Christin Johnson. George is running for re-election unopposed in District 4 {in_list}{wth_early}.
Party labels: Cave and Johnson are listed without a party; George is listed as a Republican {in_list}{incitizen_list}. In 2022 all Shoals board candidates ran without party labels {enr_2022}.

Budget and the 2025 property-tax law: at a December 29, 2025 special meeting the board unanimously approved additional appropriations and a transfer from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund. The minutes say the transfer was 'essential at this time, given the long-term impact of SB1 on the operations fund,' and that a board member noted the school will receive less funding in 2026 than in 2024 {sh_min_2025_12_29}. In April 2026 the superintendent said 'changes in enrollment, state funding, and rising costs are already impacting the budget' {sh_min_2026_04_09}. In August 2026 the board reduced a 2026 Rainy Day Fund appropriation from $600,000 to $150,000 {sh_min_2026_08_13}.

2027 budget: the published notice lists a total budget of $11,155,136. It proposes a Debt Service levy of up to $2,468,578, compared with a current levy of $1,001,543, and an Operations levy of up to $2,150,000, compared with $1,833,782 {sh_budget_notice}. No members of the public commented at the September 10 hearing or the October 8 adoption meeting, and the board adopted the budget 5-0 on October 8, 2026 {sh_min_2026_09_10}{sh_min_2026_10_08}.

Facilities and bond: in May 2025 the board voted 5-0 to move forward with an investment in facility improvements and expanded career and technical education (CTE). Then-Superintendent Hovis said the next bond could add about $6 million to the previous $3.4 million bond, for a total of $9.4 million, for CTE space, the culinary kitchen, the multipurpose room and accessible restrooms {sh_min_2025_05_22}. Preliminary determination hearings followed in July and August 2026. On August 13 the board voted 4-0 to adopt the project, preliminary determination and reimbursement resolutions, and on October 8 it approved a bond resolution 5-0 {sh_min_2026_07_09}{sh_min_2026_08_13}{sh_min_2026_10_08}. A hearing is set for November 12, 2026 on a 22-year lease to renovate part of Shoals High School. The lease sets maximum annual rental of $1.5 million, funded by property-tax bonds {sh_lease_notice}. Shoals is not listed among districts with referendums on the November 2026 ballot {dlgf_ref}.

Safety: the district completed a FEMA-standard tornado shelter attached to the high school in February 2026. It holds two classrooms and has a capacity of 368 people, and grant funding covered a substantial portion of the cost {wbiw_fema}. The board approved the shelter policy in August 2026 {sh_min_2026_08_13}.

Academics: at the April 9, 2026 meeting the middle school administration reported on a Ball State University 'value-added' study. Based on 2025 8th-grade ILEARN results, it placed Shoals in the bottom quintile: 19.4% actual proficiency against a predicted 42% {sh_min_2026_04_09}. The minutes say staff professional development then focused on 'changing the culture of our school and community to adopt a growth mindset' {sh_min_2026_04_09}.

Programs and staffing: a large crowd attended the May 27, 2026 meeting, where the superintendent said there was 'no plan to close the farm, eliminate the welding program, or disrupt the construction trades classroom' {sh_min_2026_05_27}. On June 11, 2026 the board approved ending the employment of three staff members for 2026-27 by a 3-2 vote, with Taylor and Jones voting no {sh_min_2026_06_11}. Shoals takes part in COSMOS, a partnership with Mitchell and Orleans schools for shared courses and career pathways {wbiw_cosmos_2026}. The board was told in August 2026 that 'Mitchell School will be leaving COSMOS next year' {sh_min_2026_08_13}.

Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or news profile for the Shoals races. The Washington Times Herald listed the candidates in its October 7, 2026 early-voting article {wth_early}.

Budget & taxes: part of the unanimous December 2025 vote approving additional appropriations and the Education-to-Operations Fund transfer tied to SB1 {sh_min_2025_12_29}; seconded adoption of the 2027 budget on October 8, 2026, which passed 5-0 {sh_min_2026_10_08}.

Facilities: voted for the May 2025 facility and CTE investment (5-0) {sh_min_2025_05_22}. Moved to adopt the preliminary determination resolution for the building project and co-sponsored the reimbursement resolution in August 2026 (4-0) {sh_min_2026_08_13}. Seconded the October 2026 bond resolution (5-0) {sh_min_2026_10_08}.
Staffing: the June 11, 2026 vote ending the employment of three staff members passed 3-2, with only Taylor and Jones recorded as voting no {sh_min_2026_06_11}.
